info.name: Veltrixair.com — Backend
info.description:
Backend API for veltrixair.com.

MODULES
- Discovery: 45-minute architect sessions for /talk-to-architect/ — slots, availability and booking
- Files: uploads with magic-byte validation, signed downloads, retention
- Contact: enquiry submission + admin triage for /contact-us/
- Insights: article card grid for /insights/ (cards only — no article bodies or detail pages)
- Careers: job listings + admin CRUD for /careers/ (Scope A — no applications or resume upload; the live site routes applications to careers@veltrixair.com)

GETTING STARTED
1. Start the API: npm run start:dev
2. Run "Careers > Admin > List all roles" and "Contact > Admin > List enquiries" once — they populate {{jobId}} and {{enquiryId}} for the other requests.

NOTE: admin routes are currently unauthenticated. Once the identity module lands they will require a staff bearer token.

## Authentication

Admin routes require a bearer token. Open the **Auth** folder, set the `adminPassword` collection variable, and run **Login** — the token is captured into `accessToken` and every admin request inherits it automatically.

Create the first account with `npm run admin:create -- --email you@veltrixair.com --name "Your Name" --role SUPER_ADMIN --generate`.

### Token renewal

Access tokens last 15 minutes. A collection pre-request script renews them automatically about a minute before expiry, the same way a frontend HTTP interceptor would — so you sign in once and keep working. Watch the Postman console for "Access token auto-refreshed".

Your session lasts as long as the refresh token: 7 days. After that, or if a refresh token gets replayed, sign in again from the Auth folder.

### Sites

One backend serves three brands. Public routes work out which one from the
request origin — but every request here comes from {{baseUrl}}, which belongs
to no brand, so a pre-request script sends X-Site-Code from the `siteCode`
collection variable (default 101, Veltrixair IT). The Crane Quotes folder
overrides it to 102 on each request.

Admin routes ignore that header entirely: their brand is signed into the token
at login, which is why Login takes a siteCode. Set the variable and sign in to
the matching brand, or admin lists will look empty.

item.name: Staff
item.description:
Staff accounts and the roles they hold. Every route needs the ADMINS feature, which only SUPER_ADMIN carries — sign in as a super admin from the Auth folder first.

Note what is NOT here: there is no way to change what a role *means*. The role→permission matrix is read-only (see "List roles") and changes only by migration, so widening a role stays a reviewed act.

Guard rails you can test: you cannot change your own roles or deactivate yourself, an account cannot be left with zero roles, and the last active SUPER_ADMIN cannot be demoted or deactivated.

Every role assignment is a **badge**: a role on one brand. The same person may hold the same role on two brands, or two roles on one brand — each is a separate badge, and each needs its own sign-in to use.

item.name: Crane Quotes
item.description:
Request a Quote — veltrixairindustries.com/quote/ (site 102).

The largest form in the system: five sections, ~50 fields. Two things are worth understanding before you send anything.

**Section 04 is conditional.** Six questionnaires, one per service line, and only one applies. It travels as a JSON string in `scopeDetail`, and is validated against the schema for the service line you picked — an unknown key, an unknown value, or an answer from a different service line is a 400. Run "Quote options" to see which questions belong to which line.

**Priority is derived, not submitted.** Urgency is asked of everyone; the P1 question only appears for breakdown response. So urgency is the primary signal — someone can pick Installation + Emergency and never see the P1 question, and they still route as P1.

Admin routes need CRANE_QUOTES (108), held by SALES and SUPER_ADMIN, with VIEWER able to read. Sign in with `siteCode: 102`.

item.description:
"Bring an engineer, before we bring a quote." — veltrixairindustries.com/site-visit/

Simpler than the quote form despite being a similar size: no conditional questionnaire, so no JSONB, and no file upload, so ordinary JSON rather than multipart.

**Eight of the dropdowns are reused from the quote form** — service line, industry, city, access regime, crane type, OEM, environment, lead source. The two pages render them slightly differently, but a crane is a crane whichever form you arrived on, and two near-identical tables is how you add an OEM to one and forget the other.

Admin routes need CRANE_SITE_VISITS (109) — its own feature rather than the quote pipeline's, because the page describes visits as engineer-led and quotes as sales-led. Held by SALES and SUPER_ADMIN today.

exec: // Tell the backend which brand a PUBLIC request belongs to.
// In production each site is resolved from its own domain, so the frontends
// send nothing. Here every request comes from {{baseUrl}}, which belongs to
// no brand — without this header public routes return 400. Admin routes are
// skipped: their brand comes from the signed token, and a header must never
// add, not upsert: a request that sets its own brand (the Crane folder
// sends 102) must keep it rather than be overwritten by the default.
// Auto-refresh the access token before it expires.
// Mirrors what a frontend HTTP interceptor does, so the 15-minute access
// token lifetime stays invisible while testing. Refresh tokens are single
// use, so both values are rewritten together on every renewal.
// Only admin routes carry a token, and the auth routes must not be
// intercepted: login has no token yet, and refresh/logout would recurse.
console.warn("No refresh token yet — run Auth > Login first.");
// Renew a minute early so a token cannot expire mid-flight.
body: { mode: "raw", raw: JSON.stringify({ refreshToken: refreshToken }) },
// 403 means the refresh token was already spent — the server treats
// a replay as a compromise and revokes the whole family. Logging in
// again is the only way forward, and that is intended.
"Auto-refresh failed (" + (res ? res.code : err) + "). Run Auth > Login again."
